boundary: The Error-subtrait behind the six field-accessor parents is not named anywhere in the binary: no string or panic Location names it, and its method bodies are generic glue (delegation shims, a TypeId-keyed field lookup, drop glue). Its vtable layout, group structure and construction neighbourhood (vendored hyper/tokio-openssl connect stack) are pinned; its source-level name is not recoverable.

For the native-tls enum parents the variant-to-arm correspondence of the source() slots is pinned only at the level of the observed words: word 0x8000000000000000 yields (self+8, io vtable), a small/pointer word yields (self+0, ErrorStack vtable), 0x8000000000000001 and words >= 0x8000000000000002 yield None.  Which named variant owns the small-word arm is not asserted: the Debug jump table maps the small-word arm to Ssl (formatting the value at +0x20) while the accessor returns the word at +0 as an ErrorStack.

The pair-store and pair-clone bodies are large functions (215-3229 bytes) with no panic Location of their own except 0x2e7db50 (socket2 socket.rs:105 and the hyper-fork HTTP connect code); their argument/return shapes and the two construction xrefs into the field-parent family are pinned, their source-level identities are not.

Three slot bodies are shared between the io vtables of the census packet and these parents (the +0x38 TypeId writer 0x14c5950, the +0x40 description body 0x14c5750, the +0x50 provide body 0x14c58a0).  They appear here only as slot-role evidence for the parents; the io-vtable census itself is PR #3141's subject and is not re-claimed.
